A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in leading-order chiral effective theory, two-nucleon matrix elements are cutoff-independent at leading order in chiral perturbation theory, but not at leading order in 1 / r.
, at leading order in chiral effective field theory, the two-nucleons are not renormalizable.
, in leading-order effective field theory, two-nucleon matrix elements are independent of the short-distance cutoff used for the two-nucleons system, provided the operators are of the form 1 / r 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leading-order two-nucleon wave function in chiral effective field theory can be used to evaluate two-nucleon matrix elements of operators that scale as 1 / ( r m ) for m = 1, 2, 3.
